newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Dillon Read cuts Sears.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Dillon Read cuts Sears.

text.p: -- Dillon Read analyst Peter Schaeffer said in a research note that he lowered his recommendation on Sears, Roebuck and Co to neutral from buy due to Sears' announcement that it will refund millions of dollars to holders of its credit card who filed for bankruptcy but still made payments to Sears.
-- Sears said the repayments may have a material impact on its 1997 earnings but could not say how much of an impact that might be.
-- The analyst said he cut his rating "due to the uncertainty of the situation and our inability to effectively predict the cost of the restitution plan and any other potential damages ... ."
-- "At this point, the company is unable to determine the cost of this plan as well as the potential for additional penalties, fines or damages resulting from its actions," Schaeffer wrote.
-- Schaeffer told Reuters that he will revise his earnings estimates of $3.60 per share in 1997 and $4.15 per share in 1998 once Sears provides guidance on the plan's cost.
-- He added that his current earnings estimates do not include an anticipated $0.25 per share gain he said will be added to Sears 1997 earnings from an accounting rule change.
-- The payments are expected to cost Sears $0.15 per share per $100 million of restitutiton, the analyst said.

-- "According to the company, Sears experienced $2.3 billion in (cardholder) bankruptcy filings over a five-year period (from 1992 to date), with $400 million of the total in reaffirmed debt. At this point, the company has not identified what portion of the $400 million is in violation of bankruptcy court approval," Schaeffer said.
-- In late-session NYSE trade Thursday, Sears shares were off 3-3/8 to 47-1/2.
